title: HEIC2PNG
subtitle: Image Format Converter
description: Turns iPhone HEIC photos into PNG from the CLI, a shell pipe or Python. A small tool for a small, recurring annoyance.
longDescription: Convert iPhone HEIC photos to PNG or JPEG through Python, a CLI or shell pipes. A Pillow / pillow-heif implementation handles transparency, with explicit quality controls for PNG palette reduction and JPEG output.
mascotLines: Before 1.2.2, photo.jpg could have a PNG inside. File names are honest now.
The default PNG keeps 204 of 155,763 colours. Use -q 100 if you liked the other 155,559.
imageCaptions: -q 100 keeps all 155,763 colours; the default -q 80 leaves 204 and turns the lights grey
features: CLI, Python API and shell-pipe input/output
why: iPhones save photos as HEIC, and a lot of software still won't open them. heic2png turns them into PNG or JPEG from a command, a shell pipe or Python, with nothing to compile. HEIC is a perfectly good format; the trouble is everyone else.
gains: Converts one photo, a folder (with a shell loop) or bytes already in memory, such as an upload, without temporary files. The README's quality table also ends the guessing: -q 100 keeps every colour, -f jpg gives the smallest file.
lessons: Any PNG quality below 100 means a palette of at most 256 colours: at the default -q 80 the sample photo drops from 155,763 colours to 204.
For photos, JPEG is the small option: 2.1 MB, against 6.5 MB for the default palette PNG, and smaller even than the 2.4 MB HEIC it came from.
Up to 1.2.2, -o photo.jpg got PNG data under a .jpg name; now the file name and the contents agree.
